title: Linear transformations and coordinates in a basis
section: Linear Transformations ▷ Linearity and Component Vectors
terms: linear transformation; linear map; linear operator; component vector; coordinate vector; image of a basis.

exposition.text:
A map T : V → W is linear if T(u +v) = T (u) +T (v) and T (cu) = cT(u). If V = W it is a linear
operator. Every linear map sends zero to zero, though this alone does not prove linearity. Given
an ordered basis B = (b , . . . , b ), the coordinate vector [x] records the unique coefficients in

a coordinate vector is generally different from the original vector in standard coordinates.
Prescribing images on a dependent list defines a linear map only if every dependence relation
among inputs is respected by the outputs. After prescribing compatible images on r indepen-
dent vectors in an n-dimensional domain, an m-dimensional codomain leaves m(n − r) free scalar
parameters, one arbitrary output vector for each basis vector still unspecified.

For which real a can a linear map T : R → R satisfy T(1, 0) = (1, 2), T(0, 1) = (2, −1), and
T (1, 1) = (a, 1)?
(A) No real a (B) a = 1 only (C) a = 2 only (D) a = 3 only (E) Every real a

solution.text:
The first two input vectors form a basis, so their assigned images define one linear map.
Linearity forces T (1, 1) = (1, 2) + (2, −1) = (3, 1). Thus the third assignment is compatible
exactly for a = 3.

solution.text:
Evaluation and differentiation are linear, and so is their stated linear combination. The
other maps violate additivity or scalar homogeneity: the translation does not send zero to
zero, squares and products scale quadratically, and absolute value fails for negative scalars.

Linear maps T : R → R satisfy T (1, 1, 0) = 0, T (0, 1, 1) = (1, 0), and T (1, 0, −1) = (−1, 0).
How many independent real parameters describe all such maps?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 4

solution.text:
The third input is the first minus the second, and its prescribed image has the same rela-
tion, so it adds no constraint. The first two inputs are independent and can be extended to
